title: Thyroid needle biopsy
also: fine needle aspiration of the thyroid
what: Using ultrasound to guide it, a thin needle takes cells from a thyroid lump, called a nodule, to see if it is harmless.
why: When an ultrasound finds a nodule of a certain size or with worrying features.
tell_doctor: If you take blood thinners. The doctor decides whether to stop them

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually no special prep. A light breakfast is fine.

prepare.title: Neck
prepare.text: No high collar and no jewelry around your neck.

bring: The ultrasound report describing the nodule
Thyroid hormone test results, if you have them
steps: You lie on your back with a roll under your shoulders, so your head tilts back
The doctor finds the nodule on ultrasound and cleans the skin
Sometimes a local numbing injection is given
Cells are taken with a thin needle a few times, a few seconds each
You are asked not to swallow or talk while the needle is in
A pad is pressed on the spot
feel: It feels like a regular injection
You may feel pressure in your neck
after: Keep pressing the pad for 10 to 15 minutes
A small bruise or soreness is normal and goes away in 1 to 2 days
Results usually come in 5 to 10 days
red_flags: Neck swelling that grows fast, or trouble breathing or swallowing: call emergency services right away

faq.q: Can a biopsy spread the cells?
faq.a: No, that is a myth. A needle biopsy is a standard, safe way to find out what a nodule is.
